subject: Priv deploy stewardship & evidence routing — Order Form redlines
messages:
From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@theraplex.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: matt.dunne@theraplex.com, it_ops@theraplex.com
Date: 2026-12-19T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Private deployment stewardship & evidence routing — initial questionnaire

Vanessa,

Thanks for the demo last week — we remain excited about Redwood for our on-prem inference hosting. Procurement and IT pushed a few items we need to resolve before we can sign the Order Form/SOW. High level asks:

- We need clarity on who holds operator credentials and the proposed custody model for operator accounts during a private deployment (on-prem + VPC).
- Evidence delivery: Theraplex requires a reproducible path for transfer of snapshots and an acceptance checklist for restored environments. We’re being asked to document the chain-of-custody and validation steps.
- Escrow-like option: our legal team wants to understand what, if any, mechanisms Redwood supports (third-party escrow, quarterly encrypted snapshots to a designated depositor, or 'witness certification' by a neutral engineer).

Attached is our preliminary Security Controls Questionnaire (SCQ). Can you confirm which of these options Redwood would accept, and what the timelines look like for embedding any agreed language into the MSA (or an annex/addendum)? Also please include any suggested language for the Order Form to capture acceptance criteria.

We’ve tentatively targeted the end-of-January as a hard procurement deadline.

Thanks,
Emma Jones
Procurement Lead, Theraplex
emma.jones@theraplex.com
+1 415-555-0142

Attachment: Theraplex_Security_Controls_Questionnaire.pdf

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@theraplex.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-19T11:01:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment stewardship & evidence routing — initial questionnaire

Emma — thanks for the clear summary and the SCQ. Looping in Karthik (commercial) and Laura (legal) so we can propose a consolidated path forward. Quick notes from my side: 

1) Custody model (operator credentials): three practical options we typically propose —
   a) Customer-held operator credentials (preferred for regulated workloads): Redwood provides operator runbooks and remote witness capability; customer retains keys in their KMS.
   b) Stewarded operator with dual-control: Redwood operates certain maintenance tasks under a documented dual-auth flow; credentials rotated and escrowed to a mutually agreed-fiduciary after each major update.
   c) Temporary operator access during onboarding with audited session logs and automatic revocation post-handoff.

2) Evidence transfer & acceptance: we recommend an Exhibit in the MSA that defines a "Snapshot Acceptance Checklist" (hashes, test queries, controlled boot sequence, and verification window). We can map your SCQ items to that checklist and include an Order Form SOW bullet that requires acceptance testing by Theraplex within a 10-day window.

3) Escrow-like mechanism: we can offer either (i) quarterly encrypted snapshots pushed to a customer-designated S3 with KMS wrapping, (ii) transfer to an agreed escrow vendor, or (iii) a witnessed certification process with a Redwood engineer and a Teraplex engineer signing an acceptance form. Each has different operational overheads — I attached a short redline proposal that captures the three options and a suggested lightweight clause for the MSA.

Next steps: Laura will propose legal language and a short timeline for internal approvals. Karthik will capture the commercial implications for the Order Form (pricing for snapshot storage, retention, and witness sessions). Once we have that, we can do a 30-minute sync with your legal/IT ops to close outstanding items.

Attaching: redline_proposal_v1.docx

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

Attachment: redline_proposal_v1.docx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@theraplex.com>, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-20T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment stewardship & evidence routing — initial questionnaire

Emma — thanks for flagging. From a commercial & delivery perspective:

- Deal: THP-4721 (Order Form draft v3 in HubSpot).
- Snapshot storage pricing: quarterly encrypted snapshot push to customer-designated bucket — add-on at a fixed monthly storage fee + egress contingency for restores.
- Witness sessions: 2 hours of engineering time per certification at a fixed fee; optional recurring quarterly witness certification.

We typically recommend option (ii) for customers who want an independent custody guarantee (third-party escrow) and option (iii) — witnessed certification — for lower-friction agreements where the customer controls critical keys. Both are implementable by end of January if legal signoff is quick.

Link to the draft Order Form: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/THP-4721 (internal)

If you’re available, I propose a 30-min call Thursday 12/22 10:00–10:30 PST to run the acceptance criteria and commercial impacts. Vanessa — can you confirm host?

Karthik Iyer
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@theraplex.com>, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-20T14:37:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment stewardship & evidence routing — initial questionnaire (MSA addendum redlines)

Emma — thanks for the SCQ and the constructive dialogue. I took Vanessa’s draft and produced an annotated set of redlines for an MSA Addendum (attached). Key legal points summarized below: 

1) License scope: we will grant Theraplex a perpetual, non-transferable license to run specified model artifacts in the customer-controlled environment described in the Order Form. We will not expand to broader distribution rights without a separate license.

2) Custody & keys: if Theraplex elects customer-held credentials (option a), Redwood will not require access keys for day-to-day operations. If the parties agree to stewarded operator access (option b), we propose dual-control with audit logs and a documented handback process; credential escrow to a named fiduciary (if requested) will be limited to cryptographic material needed to restore runtime images and not to customer data.

3) Evidence transfer & acceptance criteria: the Addendum includes an Exhibit A (Snapshot Acceptance Checklist). The checklist defines test payloads, hash verification, environment boot validation, and an acceptance sign-off form, with a 10-business-day validation window. Failure to accept within the window triggers a dispute path but does not automatically reject the commercial close (we added mitigations).

4) Escrow: we are open to naming an industry-standard escrow vendor; we propose limited-scope escrow deposits (runtime snapshot + cryptographic keys required to instantiate) with an explicit release trigger (bankruptcy, insolvency, or Redwood’s inability to support the deployment). Any escrow arrangement will require an executed escrow agreement with the vendor.

5) Timing: legal can turn around a negotiated Addendum in ~7 business days after we receive Theraplex’s preferred option and any required contact for the escrow vendor. Please note that escrow takes additional time (vendor onboarding ~3–4 weeks).

I’ve annotated the redlines with comments where we need Theraplex input (custody contact, escrow vendor preference, and acceptable retention period for snapshots).

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Attachment: MSA_Addendum_redline_annotated.pdf

From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@theraplex.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-22T16:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment stewardship & evidence routing — next steps and clarifications

Thanks Vanessa/Karthik/Laura — the summary is very helpful. A couple of clarifications from our side before the Thursday call: 

- Custody: Theraplex leans to customer-held credentials for production, with a one-time stewarded access window during onboarding (option c). We need explicit language that operator passwords and long-lived keys are never escrowed unless release triggers (bankruptcy/insolvency).
- Acceptance criteria: can Redwood provide a short sample Acceptance Checklist (we saw Laura’s Exhibit A reference but would like a 1-page checklist we can share with internal stakeholders prior to legal review)?
- Escrow vendors: do you have three vendor references you’ve worked with? If so please share contact names for procurement to vet.

We’ll take the 10-day validation window; that’s workable, though we’ll need the sample checklist today if possible to circulate to our engineering and procurement teams. Attached is our IT org chart (makes clear who to include on the call).

Available times for the call: Thu 12/22 10:00–10:30 PST (as proposed) or Fri 12/23 09:00–09:30 PST. Please confirm.

Regards,
Emma Jones
Procurement Lead, Theraplex
